title: Isaiah Morgan's band, then Bourbon Street jobs with George Lewis and Smilin' Joe
summary: Isaiah took over Sam Morgan's band and Purnell toured two or three years; afterwards he worked early Bourbon Street trios, an army camp job with George Lewis, and the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You get your coke and stuff and drink. You have to keep talking. That's right.
And so they hired me with the band and gave me a tryout. Well I was pretty good on my chords. Isaiah was very strict. He wanted a rhythm section to play rhythm.
He's back in town now. He's back in town now? Yeah.

Well I worked with Isaiah oh two, three years. And I never would come home with any money. We used to play percentage jobs. When we were on a trip some of the jobs were percentage. Some of them were paid jobs and different things. But as far as I got the money I wanted to have plenty for it and I'd spend it. But anyhow I got a lot of band experience with Isaiah. And then after I left Isaiah's band I began to get a little trios. And my singing helped me out most because I never could play too much solo work. And I used to sing. I played, I remember playing a job before Bourbon Street was Bourbon Street. They had two places on Bourbon Street. Bourbon Street was a residential. They didn't have anything around Bourbon. And until Sturryville was completely closed because after it was supposed to be closed the people were over there illegal you know. And I worked on Bourbon with this Albert Walkers, they called Albert Fernandez. We had Lionel Turrigano who also played drum with, a young guy like me played drum with Isaiah Morgan too. He was my friend. And we worked the thrill there. Which we worked for about three or four years. And after I left that job, then I used to work jobs with George Lewis. Used to play different jobs. I remember one time that I got a job for some girls to dance. It was during the war. And we went around the army camp and it was a drummer by the name of Robert Davis and myself and I had George Lewis to play with us. And we stood on that job about two or three weeks. But then things was too bad over there for me. So we came on back home. And then I got jobs playing singles. And then I was playing in the evening at the house that Jack built which was on Bourbon. Bourbon was building up now. And right on the corner the famous door opened up and Smiley and Joe had the band and their piano player left. And I went and worked with Smiley and Joe. And I was working day and night. I had this day job working playing cocktail hours and that night. I worked that for about two months but man that was too hard. So I continued playing with Smiley and Joe and then I would, when George Lewis would get jobs or something like that they would hire me. I played several jobs with Keith Howard. And by this time I was getting pretty good on chords and one of the things I had to do in these little country towns playing with bands, the pianos were so bad that a piano player had the cross chord. And I was interested in it and it was very easy for me to cross chord. Sometimes I was playing in F sharp and B natural, things like that, which very few piano players
could do. You were playing with a different key than the rest of the band. That's right, with the rest of the band. You could raise up the pitch.
